source.title: Residual Tensor Train: a Flexible and Efficient Approach for Learning Multiple Multilinear Correlations
source.authors: Yi-Wei Chen; Y. Pan; Daoyi Dong

record.file_problem: The full text is present. The title in the supplied metadata differs from the title printed in the paper; the paper itself is the Residual Tensor Train study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives initialization conditions for signal and gradient stability in tensor-train models and reports training-convergence outcomes, bearing on V4 by a different model and analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports MNIST and Fashion-MNIST classification results, but the tables give test accuracy, not training classification error. The training-stability comparison is described in text and Figure 6. Theoretical stability conditions are derived for TT and ResTT; results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual connections and mean-field initialization analysis to develop tensor-train models. These multilinear models lack nonlinear activations and are outside the plain neural-network settings named by V4 and the convolutional-network settings named by V3. Its comparisons also change architecture rather than isolate initialization. No result directly tests a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: residual connections with mean-field-guided initialization improve tensor-train stability and convergence, and ResTT performs well on the tested tasks. However, the displayed convergence evidence is test accuracy versus epochs, and the experiments do not isolate initialization from architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses tensor-train models and a mean-field stability analysis, rather than the initialization interventions and plain-network settings in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Model type and virtual bond dimension; the authors report different training stability for MeanTT and ResTT and different convergence behavior at r = 20 versus r = 100.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report unstable MeanTT behavior at r = 20 and faster ResTT convergence on MNIST. Figure 6 plots test accuracy against epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual tensor-train models can achieve faster and more stable test-accuracy convergence than plain tensor-train models under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The mean-field analysis derives a unit slope-factor condition for TT and a much-smaller-than-one slope-factor condition for ResTT, attributing the relaxed condition to residual connections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections relax initialization conditions for signal and gradient propagation in tensor-train models.

record.problems: Training-stability outcomes are described qualitatively and by Figure 6; no uncertainty is stated for these outcomes. The MeanTT–ResTT comparison does not isolate initialization from residual connections. The image-classification tables report test accuracy, not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Table II and Tables IV–V report test accuracy rather than the training-error behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size, regularization, or stopping effects.
Spurious local minima and student overparameterization in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation and identity-shortcut comparisons in convolutional networks; deep plain tanh and Fixup results.
Activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; orthogonal convolution kernels.
Loss and curvature behavior relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on learning speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons. TT-BN test accuracy does not measure these effects.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its different model class and measures do not constitute a limitation of V4; they leave V4 untested.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, training classification error, and the stated model-size and training-duration conditions.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons in plain and residual convolutional networks, identity shortcuts in those networks, and Fixup or special initialization in deep plain networks.
Plain neural networks with activation-matched initialization; tanh networks and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights; orthogonal convolution kernels and 10,000-layer networks.
Learning-rate behavior above the stability limit, loss and curvature trajectories, and edge-of-stability training.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance in the specified model and dataset settings.

rows.subject: MeanTT
rows.operation_detail: Compared training convergence and stability against ResTT on MNIST with limited training data.

conditions.value: not stated in the Figure 6 description
MeanTT initialized using the stability condition derived in Sec. IV-A

rows.measure: Training stability and convergence across epochs
rows.baseline: ResTT converges to an approximately optimal point within just 20 epochs.
rows.value: The training of MeanTT with r = 20 is highly unstable on a fraction of data.
rows.note: The comparison includes residual connections as well as initialization differences, so it does not isolate initialization's effect.
rows.check: MeanTT is a multilinear tensor-train model, not the activation-based plain networks named by V4. Figure 6 measures test accuracy versus epochs, not training loss or training classification error. The authors describe unstable training, but that description does not establish an incomplete V4 effect. Figure 6 includes 1%, 5%, 10%, and 100% training fractions.

rows.subject: ResTT
rows.operation_detail: Compared training convergence against MeanTT on MNIST with limited training data.

conditions.value: not stated in the Figure 6 description
proper initialization guided by the mean-field analysis

rows.value: ResTT with r = 100 takes only about 5 epoches to complete the training.
rows.note: The comparison includes residual connections as well as initialization differences; the authors describe the result as convergence, not training classification error.
rows.check: This is performance of the proposed residual tensor-train method, outside V4's system and intervention. The approximately five-epoch convergence statement is supported by test-accuracy trajectories in Figure 6(b); it does not establish completion of training by a training-objective measure. Architecture and initialization are not separated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
